explanation: Visit cells down a column, then advance to the next column. Leave clues unchanged. For each zero cell, try digits 1 through n after scanning its row, column and square region for conflicts; recurse and undo a failed assignment.
timeComplexity: O(n^(e+2) + n²) conservative worst-case time for e empty cells in an n×n board: up to n^e search nodes, up to n candidate digits and O(n) conflict scanning per node, plus traversal of fixed cells. Each recursive choice fills an empty cell, giving at most n choices at each of e branching levels; the local candidate-check cost multiplies that tree size.
spaceComplexity: O(n²) recursion frames in the worst case as all n² cells can remain on the call stack; the board is mutated in place and no candidate tables are allocated. Each live recursive call and retained candidate structure is counted; the board itself belongs to the caller.
attribution: Unmodified reference from epi_judge_python_solutions/sudoku_solve.py; Elements of Programming Interviews Judge contributors; CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 International, retained in repository LICENSE. Explanation authored for EPI Practice.
correctness: The board is a valid partial assignment before each recursive call. A candidate absent from its row, column and region preserves that invariant. Every legal digit is tried, so any completion is reachable; failure resets the cell to zero before returning. The wrapper checks the mutated board and preserved clues, not the method’s boolean.
walkthrough: For [[1,0,0,4],[0,4,1,0],[0,1,4,0],[4,0,0,1]], the column-first traversal skips clue 1, assigns 2 at (1,0), then 3 at (2,0). Completing and backtracking as needed gives a valid board such as [[1,3,2,4],[2,4,1,3],[3,1,4,2],[4,2,3,1]]. The callable returns true on success, but the executable case’s true is the wrapper verdict after checking every unit and clue.
edgeCases: A fully solved board requires no assignments.
Subgrid width is the square root of the valid board dimension, including 4 by 4 boards.
Only zero cells are changed; a dead-end branch must undo its tentative digit before trying another.
